Upgradation of MIG Jets 
*142.     SHRI R.P. GOENKA: 
SHRI SAHSH PRADHAN:† 
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleasecfto state: 
(a) whether Government are planning to upgrade the entire fleet of MIG 
jets (MIG 23 and MIG 29) through the Russian Aircraft Corporation MIG, 
vho have designed and developed the aircraft; 
(b) if so, whether addjuate detailed studies/tests have been carried out to ensure 
that the upgraded jets would meet the new strategic challenges in the sky in the 
region; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether, and to what extent, it would be a viable economic proposition as 
compared to the next generation jets available in the international market? 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES): (a) No, 
Sir. Only MIG-21 Bis are being upgraded through Russia. 
(b) and (c) Studies have been conducted to ensure that the upgraded aircraft would 
adequately meet the strategic challenges of the future. Based on the detailed studies, 
it has been planned to upgrade the aircraft, which would include advanced avionics 
and Electronic Warfare systems, modem weapons systems, enhancement in range 
with air-to-air refuelling, enhancement in operational capability through integration 
of new weapons etc.

Scientific Method to prevent Casualties in Mining Sector 
*147. MISS MABEL REBELLO : Will ihe Minister of COAL be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether Coal India Limited (CIL) have introduced scientific methods 
to prevent casualties is the mining sector; 
(b) if so, the extent to which fatality rate in coal mining sector has been 
reduced during the last three years; 
(c) whether due to lack of co-ordination between the CIL and DGMS, the 
implementation of safety norms in coal sector have not proved effective; and 
(d) if so, the facts thereof and Government's further reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF COAL (SHRI N.T. 
SHANMUGAM): (a) to (d) Coal India has introduced several systems for 
bringing down the accident rate in its coal mines which includes improvement, 
in support system of underground mines, reduction in exposure of men to risk 
by mechanisation and increasing the share of opencast mining etc. 
Fatality rates in coal mines arc adjudged on the basis of fatality rate per 
million tonne of production and fatality rate per three (3) lakh manshift 
deployed. On both these counts the fata lity rale has drastically reduced after 
the formation of Coal India Ltd., and is  still continuing its downward trend. 
In 1975 fatality rate per million tonne production was 2.62 which is now 
0.43, 0.40 and 0.39 in the years 1997, 1998 and 1999 respectively. Similarly, 
fatality rate per three (3) lakh manshift deployed stood at 0.52 in 1975 which 
has now come down to 0.25 and 0.24 in the year 1997 and 1998 / 99. 
There is no lack of co-ordination between Directorate Genera! of Mines 
Safety (DGMS) and Coal India Limited on safety matters. The safety norms/ 
rules formulated by DGMS are implemen ted in Coal India Limited mines. 
Safety Board meetings at Coal India are held twice in a year which have 
representation from DGMS. Tripartite meetings between management, DGMS 
and Trade Union representatives are held twice in a year at subsidiary Company 
level and once in a year at Colliery/ Unit level. Similarly, Standing Committee 
on Safety Chaired by Minister Incharge  (Coal) arc held twice a year, in the 
Ministry of Coal, which is represented by Director General of Mines Safety 
and Ministry of Labour officials As such, there is no lack of coordination 
between Coal India and DGMS in safety matters.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (SHRI M. KANNAPPAN): (a) and 
(b) Yes Sir. India has a vast potential for the use of solar energy with an average 
incident energy from the sun of about 5,000 trillion KWH every year. This 
energy can be utilized for various applications like water heating, cooking, 
drying, lighting, pumping, power generation, etc. A number of devices and 
systems working on solar energy have been developed and are being installed 
in various parts of the coutry. The Government has taken several initiatives to 
develop and promote the use of these systems. These include the following: 
(i)   A promotional scheme through state nodal agencies, an interest free 
loan scheme through the Indian Renewable Energy Development 
Agency (IREDA) and a Self Employed Workers scheme for promoting 
solar cookers. 
(ii)  Demonstration scheme on cost sharing basis for newer technologies 
like concentrating type solar cookers for community use. 
(iii) Soft loan schemes on solar water heating systems through IREDA 
and Banks. 
(iv)  Subsidy & loan schemes on so lar photovoltaic systems through state 
nodal agencies and IREDA. 
(v)  Establishment of Aditya Solar Sh ops for sale and servicing of solar 
devices in different cities. 
(vi)  Sanctioning of R&D projects to technical institutions and industry for 
the development of solar devices. As a result of R&D efforts made in 
the country, several devices have been developed and improved and 
indigenous capacities established for manufacturing. 
(c) and (d) The Government has not imported any solar cooker or stove 
from China. The cooker being generally promoted in China is of the focussing 
type which concentrates sunlight at the bottom of the cooking pot. It can be 
used for a variety of cooking needs including frying. The cooker, however, can 
cook only one item at a time and costs around US $ 100. In India, the box type 
of solar cooker has been more common. It has the advantages of cooking 4 
items at a time and less cost (Rs. 1,200/- approx). This cooker, however, takes 
more time for cooking and cannot be used for frying. The Government has 
recently started a new scheme under which concentrating type solar cookers 
made in India are being installed in the country for purpose of demonstration. 
The cost and efficiency of these cooker s are similar to those of the Chinese 
models.

1088. SHRI CM. IBRAHIM: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) what progress has been made so far in pursuance of Government's 
policy for privatization of transmission and distribution (T and D) of power 
in different sectors, following the amendment in the Power Act;

much higher as compared to International Standards in this regard; 
and

privatization?

(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTIMEHTA): (a) The Electricity Laws (Amendment) 
Act, 1998 (Act No. 22 of 1998) recognizes Transmission as a separate 
activity. Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. as the Central Transmission 
Utility has identified the transmission system for evacuation of power from 
Tala Hydro Electric Project in Bhutan (1020 MW) and other projects under 
execution in the North-Eastem/ Eastern region for execution through Joint

POWERGRID. POWERGRID has also decided to take up one pilot project 
with 100% equity participation from private sector as an Independent Power 
Transmission Company under the guidance of a consultant appointed by the 
Asian Development Bank under their Technical Assistance Programme.

state sector is to be taken by the appropriate agencies in the States. 
Government of Orissa have privatized distribution in the State.

much higher than the T&D losses ranging between 8 to 10% in developed 
countries.

THE MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE & COMPANY AFFAIRS 
AND m 'ISTER OF SHIPPING   (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY): Sir, f move: 
"That the Bill to repeal the Civil Codes Amins Act, 1856 and 
certain other enactments, be taken into consideration.* 
The Government of India had appointed the P.C. Jain 
Committee which had gone into the question of obsolete laws. About 
1,300 laws were found obsolete by  the Committee and they still 
continue to be on the Statute Book.   A process of removing each one 
of these laws from the 
171 

RAJYA  SABHA [29 November, 2000]  
Statute Book has been undertaken. Both the Houses of Parliament have 
already repealed several of these laws. This particular Bill deals with the 
repeal of 17 such laws that have become completely obsolete. I will just 
give some Illustrations. 
The first one, the Civil Courts Amins Act, 1856 continues to be on 
the Statute Book, even though the whole system of Amins in Civil Codes 
has been abolished and Is no longer in vogue. The Bombay High Court 
(Letters Patent) Act, 1666 corrected some two clerical errors in the original 
Act and is no longer required to be on the Statute Book. The two 
Unclaimed Deposits Acts, 1866 and 1870, referred to only the jurisdiction 
within the Presidency Towns which have since been abolished and the laws 
have ceased to exist. The Acting Judges Act, 1867 has outlived its utility 
because even the Acting Judges are now regulated by article 224 of the 
Constitution and not by the 1867 regulation. The legislation, the 
Procedure of the High Court for Uttar Pradesh, is redundant because there 
is no longer a High Court of Uttar Pradesh. We have the High Court of 
ABahabad. The Presidency Magistrates (Court-fees) Act, 1877 deals with 
Presidency Towns. The Punjab Courts (Supplementing) Act, 1919 deals 
with the jurisdiction of the High Court of Lahore. The Federal Court Act, 
1937 and the Federal Court (Enlargement of Jurisdiction) Act, 1947 deal with 
the Federal Court which had ceased to exist since 1950, after the Supreme 
Court came into existence. The Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 
1949 is no longer required because the Privy Council no longer has 
jurisdiction, as far as India is concerned. The Rajasthan High Court 
Ordinance, 1949 is no longer relevant because the Rajasthan High Court, 
after the States Reorganisation Act, is now regulated by the Constitutional 
provisions. The Bhopal and Vindhya Pradesh (Courts) Act, 1950 deals with 
the jurisdiction of the erstwhile courts of Bhopal and Vindhya Pradesh. 
Now, it has already been reorganised and merged with Madhya Pradesh. 
Then, we had laws relating to the Judicial Commissioners. There is not a 
single Judicial Commissioner left in the country. The law relating to the 
jurisdiction of Mysore High Court is no longer relevant because we now 
have the Karnataka High Court which has jurisdiction over the entire State. 
Similarly, the law relating to the Manipur Court-fees Act has become 
redundant. The Judicial Commissioner's Court law in relation to Goa, 
Daman and Diu has also become redundant since the Judicial Commissions

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF HOME 
AFFAIRS (SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO): Madam 
Deputy Chairman, I move: 
        "That the  Bill  further to amend  the  Punjab Municipal 
Corporation Law (Extension to   Chandigarh) Act, 1994, as 
                passed by Lok Sabha, be taken into consideration." 
The Bill seeks to provide for the representation of a Member 
of the House of the People repr esenting the Union Territory of 
Chandigarh in the Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh with a right to 
vote. The Punjab Municipal Corporation Act of 1976 as amended by 
the State Government in May, 1994    was extended to the Union 
Territory of Chandigarh  by the Punjab Municipal Corporation Law 
{Extension to   Chandigarh) Act of 1994. The Punjab Act does not 
provide for the representation of the Member of the House of the 
People in the Municipal Corporati on and, accordingly, no provision 
was made in the said Act of 1994 for the representation of the 
member of the House of the People representing the Union Territory 
of Chandigarh in the Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh. 
Article 243R of the Constitution, inter alia, provides that the 
Legislature of the State may, by law,  provide for the representation in 
a Municipality of the Member.of the House of the People and the 
Members of the Legislative Asse mbly of the State representing 
constituencies which comprise wholly or partly the Municipal area. 
The matter about representation of local Member of 
Parliament in the Municipal Corporation Chandigarh, was raised in 
various meetings of the Departm ent-Related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Ministry of Home A ffairs during consideration of the 
Demands for Grants of the Ministry. The Committee, in its 37 ,h 
Report, had recommended that- 
“..it is hoped that the situation will be rectified and the area 
Member of Parliament will be  deemed as a member of the 
Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh, as per the provisions of the 
73rd amendment of the Constitution."

meetings held on 23 ,d and 24 m March, 1999 while examining the

"The Committee notes the reply furnished by 
the Ministry and hopes that an early decision 
on the proposals of the Ministry would be 
taken by the Government to ensure 
representation of the Local MP. in the 
Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh. The 
Committee also urges upon the Ministry to 
make the progress of case known to it from

It is in pursuance of the above recommendations of the 
Committee that the Government have moved to provide for the 
representation of the Member of Parliament from Chandigarh in the 
Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh with a right to vote. Accordingly, 
the Punjab Municipal Corporation Law (Extension to Chandigarh) Act, 
1994 is being amended.
